content: Early blight is a fungal disease caused by Alternaria solani. Symptoms: Dark, concentric rings or 'bullseye' spots on older, lower leaves. Leaves may turn yellow and drop. Stem lesions and fruit rot can also occur. Treatment: Apply copper-based fungicides or chlorothalonil. Ensure proper spacing for airflow. Use mulch to prevent soil splashing. Remove infected plant debris immediately.

Late blight is caused by Phytophthora infestans and can rapidly destroy entire crops. Symptoms: Water-soaked, irregularly shaped pale green or brown lesions on leaves. In humid conditions, a white fungal growth appears on the undersides of leaves. Stems may develop dark brown lesions. Treatment: Destroy infected plants immediately. Apply protective fungicides like chlorothalonil or mancozeb before infection spreads. Avoid overhead watering.

Leaf rust (Puccinia triticina) affects wheat. Symptoms: Small, round to oval, orange-red pustules predominantly on the upper leaf surface. Severely infected leaves die early, reducing yield. Treatment: Plant rust-resistant varieties. Apply foliar fungicides such as azoxystrobin or tebuconazole when pustules first appear, especially before the heading stage.

Northern Corn Leaf Blight (NCLB) is a fungal disease. Symptoms: Large, cigar-shaped, grayish-green to tan lesions on the leaves, initially appearing on lower leaves. Lesions can coalesce and kill entire leaves. Treatment: Use resistant hybrids. Rotate crops to non-hosts for at least one year. Tillage can help bury infected residue. Apply fungicides (e.g., strobilurins) if disease appears early in the season.

Apple scab is caused by Venturia inaequalis. Symptoms: Olive-green to black, velvety spots on leaves and fruit. Severely infected leaves yellow and drop early. Fruit may become distorted and cracked. Treatment: Sanitation is critical—rake and destroy fallen leaves. Apply preventative fungicides (like captan or myclobutanil) starting at green tip through petal fall. Choose scab-resistant apple varieties.

Powdery mildew affects many crops (cucurbits, grapes, apples). Symptoms: White or gray powdery fungal growth primarily on the upper surfaces of leaves, stems, and sometimes fruit. Leaves may twist and yellow. Treatment: Apply sulfur-based fungicides, potassium bicarbonate, or neem oil at first sign of disease. Ensure good air circulation. Avoid high nitrogen fertilizers which promote lush, susceptible growth.
